cycles.rationale: Cycle 0 with large yaw error (-62.8 deg), stable grasp, no drift, and zero spin, so start with an early coarse rotation primitive to measure its yaw gain.

action_02 slightly helped yaw but sharply worsened tilt/Y (rot_dist rose), and with a sphere showing significant Y error (-28.2 deg) plus large remaining Z error under stable drift, an untried sphere Y-orientation probe that braces fore/middle contacts is the best next correction.

The dominant error is now the negative Y/tilt component (-43.5 deg, rot_dist rising), and action_22 (thumb direction A) made Y worse, so I switch to its opposed sphere-Y probe action_23 while drift is low and stable.

The dominant error is the large negative Y component (-53.6 deg, tilt 53.8) and both tried sphere-Y probes (action_22/23) produced wrong-sign positive Y gains that worsened tilt, so the untried reverse-trajectory sphere-Y probe action_24 is the best candidate to reduce Y while drift remains low and stable.

The sphere has a very large full-orientation error (rot_dist 1.246 rad) that has stalled across four different probes while yaw gains keep worsening tilt, so the sphere large-orientation escape best matches this stalled, far-from-target state with position still stable.

The dominant error is the large negative Y component (-60.5 deg) with rot_dist still 1.29 rad, and action_24 is the only tried primitive that reduced full orientation error (rot_dist_gain +0.0247) while producing a correctly-signed negative Y gain (-10.6 deg), so repeating it best targets the dominant axis.

The dominant errors are Y (-46.7 deg) and full rot_dist (1.09 rad), and action_24 is the only probe whose measured Y and rot_dist gains are consistently helpful (last rot_dist gain +0.2022 rad with improving trend and only 2 uses), drift is stable and spin is low so no hold is needed.

Full-orientation error is still ~1.05 rad with tilt/Y dominating (-48 deg) and action_24 has been repeated with decaying, sign-wrong Y gain, so I switch to an untried three-axis X/Y orientation probe while drift remains stable.

Tilt error is large (52 deg, dominated by Y=-51.7) and action_18's direction-A probe just increased full orientation error, so I switch to the untried direction-B three-axis probe action_19 rather than repeating decaying action_24.

Tilt error (Y: -57 deg) dominates and action_24 is the only primitive with consistently positive full-orientation gains (mean +0.0895 rad, latest +0.0417 rad) while also adding positive yaw; drift and spin are low so it remains safe to continue.

The dominant residual is the large negative Y rotation error and action_24 has the strongest recent full-orientation and Y gains with stable drift, so I continue the effective sphere Y-orientation probe.

action_24 is still the strongest performer with large recent rot_dist gains (~0.11 rad) and a Y-axis gain sign (-9.508) that matches the dominant negative Y error (-39.2), while drift remains low and the action has not stalled (latest gain 0.1066 >> 0.01), so continuing it is preferable to switching to actions 22/23/25 whose Y gains have the wrong sign and worsened rot_dist.

action_24 has been used three straight cycles with decaying rot_dist gain (0.111→0.107→0.048), a negative last tilt gain, and a wrong-signed Y effect, while drift is stable (0.0189<0.02) and tilt/Y error (~40 deg) dominates, so I switch to an untried different-contact three-axis probe to address the X/Y tilt without reseating.

The dominant error is the large negative Y component (-59.5 deg) with rot_dist 1.10 rad, and action_24 has the strongest track record of reducing full-orientation error on this sphere (mean gain +0.089 rad, recent gains up to +0.111 rad), while spin is low and drift is tiny, so no hold or reseat is needed.

The dominant error is the large negative Y component (-52.9 deg, tilt 54.2) and action_24 is the only sphere-Y probe whose measured Y gain matches that sign while still reducing rot_dist (latest gain +0.123 rad, positive trend, not stalled), so I continue it despite moderate spin and stable low drift.

The dominant error is Y at -52 deg (tilt 53.7, rot_dist 0.96) and action_24 is the only tried sphere-Y probe with a correctly-signed negative Y gain and positive rot_dist gain, while actions 22/23/25 and the three-axis probes all show wrong-sign positive Y gains and negative rot_dist gains; drift is low and spin is moderate, so I continue the still-net-positive action_24 rather than switch to a harmful or untested wrong-direction probe.
action_24 has decayed after three uses (last rot_dist gain 0.0091 rad), so with stable drift and dominant X/Y tilt error I will switch to the untried contact-changing X/Y probe action_20.

Full orientation error is still large (rot_dist 1.04 rad) with dominant Y tilt (-55 deg), action_24 is flagged stalled after 9 uses and action_20 just worsened rot_dist/tilt, so I switch to an untried alternate-contact action to refresh the contact pattern and escape the stall while drift remains stable.

Last cycle action_04 produced the largest recent full-orientation improvement (rot_dist gain 0.1699 rad, tilt gain 9.692 deg) while drift stayed tiny, and the dominant remaining error is X/Y tilt on the sphere, so repeat this effective contact-changing probe once rather than switching blindly.

action_04 is the only measured action that simultaneously reduces the dominant negative Y tilt (recent Y gain -6 to -8 deg), positive X error, and full rot_dist (last gain +0.110 rad), and despite two consecutive uses its gains remain strong, so I continue it rather than gamble on an untried primitive while angular speed is low (0.216 rad/s) and drift is negligible.

The dominant error is still Y/tilt (Y=-33.4, tilt=33.8) and action_04 is the only primitive consistently reducing rot_dist (0.95->0.68) and tilt (59->34) with recent3 gains still strong (0.12 rad, Y gain same sign as the negative Y error), it is not stalled and drift is low, so I continue it rather than switching to positive-yaw actions that historically worsen full orientation.

action_04 has decayed after four straight uses (rot_dist gain down to 0.01 rad), so I switch contact groups to the thumb-based sphere-Y probe action_24, whose measured Y/Z gains are negative and match the current dominant negative Y (-29.5) and Z (-24.4) errors while keeping drift (0.021 m, z positive) acceptable.

Largest errors are Y (-21.6) and Z (-24.2), both negative; action_24's last gains (Y -7.93, Z -0.27) match those signs, cut tilt by 7.9 deg and rot_dist by 0.103 rad with positive trend and only one consecutive use, while drift is stable and spin is moderate, so continuing it is best.

action_24 is still the best-signed sphere probe: its last two uses cut rot_dist from 0.669 to 0.492 rad with positive yaw (correct for the negative err_deg) and negative gains matching the dominant negative Y/Z error components, while drift stays low and gain (0.074 rad) is far above the 0.01 stall threshold, so continuing its waveform is warranted.

action_24 has been used three consecutive cycles with rot_dist gain decaying to 0.0118 rad and tilt gain turning negative, so I switch to an untried all-finger contact-recovery action to refresh the contact pattern before the next correction while drift remains low and stable.

Drift is low and spin is modest, while action_24 is the only tried sphere Y-orientation probe with consistently positive full-orientation gain and positive yaw effect for the current negative err_deg, despite diminishing returns.

The sphere's dominant Y error (-18.3 deg) and tilt (19.2 deg) are still large with rot_dist 0.476, and action_24 is the proven sphere-Y probe whose recent rot_dist gains remain positive (last +0.0618 rad, recent3 +0.049) with negative Y-axis gain matching the negative Y error, so continue it rather than switching while drift is low and progress has not stalled.

The grasp is stable and action_24 is still the only measured primitive consistently reducing rot_dist while producing the needed positive yaw/Z correction for the sphere, with latest gain 0.047 rad so it has not stalled.

action_24 is flagged stalled after three consecutive uses (last rot_dist gain 0.0031 < 0.01) and is now worsening tilt, so I am switching to the opposite-direction sphere-Y thumb probe action_23 to attack the dominant -21.9 deg Y error while position remains stable and drift is low.
Dominant error is Y tilt (-26.9 deg); action_04 shows consistent negative Y-axis gain and positive full-orientation gain, while the Y-probe action_24 has stalled and recently pushed Y the wrong way.

Sphere tilt is dominated by Y=-16.8deg and last cycle action_04 gave the best rot_dist gain (0.1616 rad) and tilt reduction (10.0deg) with a Y gain sign matching the current negative Y error, while drift is tiny and it has only one consecutive use, so I repeat it once before switching contact groups.

The error is now balanced negative X (-8.63) and Z (-8.97) with Y near zero, action_04 has run twice consecutively and is overshooting yaw negative while action_24 is stalled, so I switch to a different three-axis probe whose measured gains [-8.79, 3.07, -2.82] match the needed negative-X/negative-Z correction with only mild Y disturbance while drift stays negligible.

rot_dist is still 0.253 rad with ~10 deg tilt and very low drift/spin, and action_04 is the only primitive that recently cut full-orientation error and tilt substantially (+0.16/+0.09 rad) without its effect decaying; the prior two-use streak was broken by action_20, so resuming it best drives rot_dist toward <0.1.

The dominant error is the X tilt component (-16.417 deg, tilt 18.6 deg) with stable grasp and moderate spin; action_18 is the X/Y orientation probe whose measured X gain (-14.321 deg) best matches reducing that negative X error, and recent action_04/action_20 repeats worsened rot_dist so a different contact group is warranted.

The dominant error is the +15.6 deg Y component (tilt 18.4 deg) while yaw is nearly settled, drift is low/stable, and action_22 is the sphere Y-probe whose measured Y gain is strongly positive (+15.3) and not in its avoid state, making it the best match to attack the largest axis without repeating the decayed action_24 or the Y-worsening action_18.

Yaw is essentially aligned but rot_dist_rad 0.334 is dominated by ~19 deg X/Y tilt with X the largest component (-15.39); action_18 is a three-axis X/Y probe whose recent use in a similar state reduced rot_dist and strongly corrects negative X error, and it is not over-repeated while drift stays near zero.
The sphere still has moderate residual spin after the last large orientation probe, so a brief zero-command hold should damp motion before the next X/Z correction.

The largest error is the negative X/tilt component with stable drift and only moderate spin, and action_18 is the X/Y probe with the best recent rot_dist and tilt gains despite needing later yaw cleanup.

The dominant +21 deg Z (yaw) error needs negative yaw, but repeated action_18 produced positive yaw (Z gain negative) and has stalled, so with stable drift I switch to an untried coarse-rotation contact group to seek a negative-yaw correction.

The large +27.8 deg yaw error needs negative yaw while X tilt is -14.6 deg, and action_15 is the only tried primitive whose measured component gains match those signs (X gain -12.9, Z gain +2.8) with negative yaw delta, reduced rot_dist (-0.057 rad) and lower tilt on a stable low-drift grasp.

The sphere's full orientation error is very large (rot_dist 0.692 rad) and recent probes have stalled or worsened it, so the dedicated little-finger large-orientation escape best matches this stalled, far-from-target sphere state while position drift remains stable.

err_deg has ballooned to +45.8 (dominant +Z) and every recent action produced positive yaw making it worse; action_04 is the only primitive with negative mean yaw (-2.98 deg) to counter the +Z error, has the best episode rot_dist gain (+0.066) and recent3 gains that help Y (-11.4) and Z (+1.15), and is not recently repeated (consecutive_recent_uses 0).

The last five primitives all made rot_dist_rad worse (0.42→1.02) while drift stays low and stable, so I abandon the failing rotation pattern and use an untried multi-finger contact-refresh (action_07) to re-establish contact before resuming correction.

Full-orientation error is still large with stable drift, and recent/stalled tried primitives mostly worsened rot_dist, so I’m exploring an untried wrist-plus-fore/middle coarse rotation from a different contact group.

Drift is still low and stable, so I’m selecting an untried thumb-led coarse rotation to attack the dominant positive Z/yaw error after recent tried primitives either stalled or worsened full orientation.

The dominant error is +Z yaw (~+49 deg) requiring negative yaw, and action_07 is the only lightly-used primitive that produced a negative measured yaw (-3.08 deg) with positive Z-axis gain; contacts are stable (low drift) so a contact-refresh/negative-yaw stroke is the best lever while avoiding the stalled action_24 and harmful action_25.

Large full-orientation error (0.978 rad) with stable drift, and action_06 produced the best recent rot_dist gain (+0.0676) and tilt reduction while matching the negative X-error direction before action_07 regressed.

Drift is stable and action_06 most recently reduced full orientation error and tilt with gains aligned to the current X/Y/Z error signs, so continuing it is safer than switching to probes that worsened rot_dist_rad.

Tilt is significant (26 deg) with error vector [-19.3,-17.6,+49.0] needing +X/+Y/-Z gains, and action_19's measured gains [+10.9,+5.3,-7.7] match all three signs while action_06 has stalled; drift is low so no reseat is needed.

The last three-axis probe action_19 (WRJ0 direction B) sharply worsened rot_dist and tilt, so with large X/Y error and low drift I select the opposite-direction three-axis probe action_18 (WRJ0 direction A), which has positive orientation gains, to recover tilt.
